title: Plan-aware fastpath allocator with quota throttling and graceful downgrade
creator: Maya Khatri
description:
Purpose: implement a plan-aware fastpath allocator that admits requests into low-latency lanes for free/paid/enterprise plans while enforcing per-plan and per-tenant quota guardrails, and providing graceful downgrade to slower but cheaper model variants when quotas are exceeded.

Scope: routing decision logic, admission controller, quota accounting hooks, telemetry events, and a staged rollout path (canary -> regional -> global). This ticket focuses on the allocator and soft-degradation policy; downstream work will integrate autoscaling and billing signals.

Goals: reduce p95 latency for enterprise/paid fastpath by 20% for short prompt lengths, keep free-tier fairness under contention, prevent quota exhaustion storms by applying probabilistic throttles and short-lived soft-demotions, and provide clear observability (per-plan admission rate, demotion ratio, latency delta).

Constraints and assumptions: token consumption accounting is eventual-consistent for legacy customers (approximate counters), fastpath slots are limited per-server and must be reserved in small increments, downgrade models are quantized variants with lower throughput but higher availability, and we must maintain privacy boundaries for Private customers (no cross-tenant borrowing).
acceptance_criteria: Allocator routes requests into fastpath, warmpath, or slowpath based on plan, current quota, and regional capacity
Under synthetic contention, paid and enterprise plans maintain >=80% fastpath admission while free is probabilistically throttled according to credits
Automatic soft-demotion triggers when tenant token consumption > 85% of short-window quota and demotion gap is annotated in traces
Telemetry emits per-tenant admission metrics, demotion_reason tag, and a sampling of request traces for failed fastpath attempts
Feature flagged rollout with canary in us-west-2 and observable rollback path
Unit and e2e tests for admission logic, quota transitions, and model fallback resolution exist and pass in CI
